items.prompt: Why use math.isqrt/perfect squares and enclosure identities in tests?

options.text: They provide independent exact references/checks under this input model
options.why: They avoid treating one approximate sqrt implementation as exact ground truth.

options.text: They prove the app has the same Python environment
options.why: Local reference checks do not establish app execution.

options.text: They guarantee all generic nonlinear roots are bracketed
options.why: The component solves only this fixed nonnegative polynomial problem.

options.text: They replace the need to review the contract
options.why: A test can pass the wrong contract if the contract is ignored.

items.explanation: Independent references and algebraic properties reduce common-mode implementation/reference mistakes within the stated scope.
